en: The original 1898 Philippine Declaration of Independence was signed by 98 delegates, including one American army officer, Captain L.M. Johnson.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of 24 senators elected nationwide and up to 300 district and sectoral representatives in the House.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, with Tagalog, Cebuano, and Ilocano being the top three most widely spoken native languages.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The Ati-Atihan Festival in Kalibo, Aklan, is held every third Sunday of January and features thousands of participants painting their bodies with black soot.
The Lumad indigenous groups in Mindanao comprise over 18 distinct ethnolinguistic tribes, making up roughly 6 percent of the total Philippine population.
The Sampaguita, the national flower, typically grows to a height of 0.5 to 3 meters and features white petals that open at night.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution has 18 articles, and Article VII specifically limits the President to a single six-year term without re-election.
Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957.
The Philippine national flag features an eight-rayed sun, representing the first 8 provinces that revolted against Spain, and three five-pointed stars.
Juan Luna's famous painting Spoliarium measures 4.22 meters by 7.67 meters, making it the largest painting in the Philippines.
During the traditional Bayanihan, 20 to 30 men use bamboo poles to carry a nipa hut, which typically weighs around 1,000 kilograms.
